Mary, Queen of Scots
MAIR-ee kween uv skots
proper noun (a queen of Scotland)
Mary Stuart (1542-1587), the Roman Catholic Queen of Scotland whose reign coincided with the Scottish Reformation and whose contest with John Knox marked the conflict of crown and Kirk.

📖 Biblical Definition

Mary, Queen of Scots (Mary Stuart, 1542-1587) was the Roman Catholic Queen of Scotland whose reign (1561-1567) coincided with the triumph of the Scottish Reformation, and whose contest with John Knox and the Reformed Kirk became a defining drama of crown against gospel. Returning from France a devout Catholic to a newly Protestant realm, Mary sought to maintain her Mass and her religion against the Reformation that Parliament had established. Knox confronted her with a boldness that has become famous, refusing to flatter the throne and insisting that subjects owe obedience to God above the commands of princes—for we ought to obey God rather than men. Her reign collapsed amid intrigue, murder, and scandal; she was forced to abdicate, fled to England, was held prisoner by Elizabeth for nineteen years, and was at last executed in 1587 for her part in plots against the English crown. The dictionary treats Mary not as a figure to be either romanticized or vilified, but as a sober case in the providence of God and the relation of conscience to authority. Two truths it holds together. First, the king's heart is in the hand of the LORD; God changeth the times and seasons, removeth kings and setteth up kings, and He overruled the contest of Mary and Knox for the establishing of the gospel in Scotland. Second, Knox's stand teaches the limits of obedience to rulers: subjects honour the magistrate, but when the magistrate commands what God forbids or forbids what God commands, they must obey God rather than men. The dictionary thus reads Mary's reign as a witness to the sovereignty of God over thrones and to the duty of conscience bound by the Word of God above the will of any earthly sovereign.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Mary Stuart (1542-1587), the Roman Catholic Queen of Scotland whose reign clashed with John Knox and the Reformed Kirk; a case in the sovereignty of God over thrones and the duty to obey God rather than men.

MARY, QUEEN OF SCOTS, proper noun. Mary Stuart (1542-1587), Roman Catholic Queen of Scotland.

Her reign (1561-1567) coincided with the triumph of the Scottish Reformation.

She sought to maintain her Mass against the Reformed Kirk and was confronted by Knox.

Forced to abdicate, she fled to England and was executed in 1587.

A case in God's sovereignty over thrones and the duty to obey God above men (Acts 5:29).

⚠️ Modern Corruption

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition; the danger is the romanticizing or vilifying of Mary that obscures the lesson of God's sovereignty over thrones and the limits of obedience to rulers.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. Popular history romanticizes Mary as a tragic, wronged heroine or vilifies her as a scheming villainess, and in either case loses the lesson her reign teaches. The dictionary reads her soberly within the providence of God. The king's heart is in the hand of the LORD, who turneth it whithersoever He will; God changeth the times and seasons and removeth and setteth up kings. The contest between the Catholic queen and the Reformed Kirk, with all its intrigue and tragedy, God overruled for the establishing of His gospel in Scotland. The throne did not master the Word; the Word, by God's sovereignty, outlasted the throne.

Mary's reign also illumines the relation of conscience to authority. Knox honoured the office of the queen yet refused to flatter her sin or surrender the gospel to her will, standing on the principle that we ought to obey God rather than men. The dictionary holds the balance Scripture teaches: subjects owe real honour and obedience to the civil magistrate, yet that obedience has a limit, for when the ruler commands what God forbids or forbids what God commands, the conscience bound by the Word must obey God first. Mary, Queen of Scots, stands as a witness both to the sovereignty of God over the thrones of the earth and to the liberty of a conscience captive to the Word of God.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Mary Stuart, of the royal house of Stewart; “Queen of Scots” the title of the Scottish crown; her reign set the Catholic throne against the Reformed Kirk.

Mary Stuart (1542-1587), of the house of Stewart.

“Queen of Scots,” the title of the sovereign of Scotland.

Reigned 1561-1567 amid the triumph of the Reformation.

Confronted by John Knox, who would not flatter the throne.

Executed in 1587 for plots against Elizabeth of England.
